name: Hydrogen combustion
jarvis: Two hydrogen molecules and one oxygen make two waters. Delta H minus five hundred and seventy two kilojoules — violently exothermic, sir.

name: Methane combustion
jarvis: Complete combustion of methane: carbon dioxide, water, and eight hundred and ninety kilojoules released per mole.

name: Ethane combustion
jarvis: Ethane burns hot and clean, sir — carbon dioxide and water only.

name: Ethene combustion
jarvis: Ethene burns with a luminous flame — the extra carbon makes it sootier than methane.

name: Haber process
jarvis: The Haber process. Iron catalyst, four hundred and fifty degrees, two hundred atmospheres. It feeds half the planet.

name: Neutralisation
jarvis: Textbook neutralisation, sir — a proton meets a hydroxide and both cancel. Salt and water, minus fifty seven kilojoules.

name: Neutralisation (KOH)
jarvis: Potassium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid. Same story, different spectator ion.

name: Limestone decomposition
jarvis: Thermal decomposition. Endothermic — you must keep feeding the kiln. Quicklime and carbon dioxide.

name: Ethene hydrogenation
jarvis: The pi bond opens and two hydrogens add across it. Nickel catalyses it beautifully.

name: Esterification
jarvis: Acid plus alcohol gives an ester and water. Concentrated sulfuric acid removes the water and drives it forward.

name: Hydrogen chloride formation
jarvis: A photochemical chain reaction, sir — one photon sets off thousands of propagations. Do not stand near it.

name: Water electrolysis
jarvis: Splitting water. Endothermic — you must pay back every joule the combustion released.

name: CO oxidation
jarvis: Exactly what your catalytic converter does, sir. Carbon monoxide in, carbon dioxide out.

name: Contact process step
jarvis: Sulfur trioxide plus water. Done directly it makes an acid mist, so industry absorbs it in concentrated acid first.

name: Sulfur dioxide oxidation
jarvis: Vanadium pentoxide catalyst. This is the step that turns pollution into acid rain — and into sulfuric acid.

name: NO₂ dimerisation
jarvis: Two radicals pair their odd electrons. Cool the brown gas and it pales as it dimerises.

name: Sodium + water
jarvis: Violently exothermic. The hydrogen ignites and the sodium skitters about like something possessed.

name: Calcium + water
jarvis: Gentler than sodium — the bubbles of hydrogen cling to the metal and float it upward. Charming, really.

name: Magnesium + acid
jarvis: The classic school reaction, sir. Magnesium disappears, hydrogen pops.

name: Ozone decomposition
jarvis: Ozone gladly falls apart into oxygen. Chlorofluorocarbons merely help it along — hence the hole.

name: Benzene hydrogenation
jarvis: Breaking aromaticity is expensive, sir — benzene resists, and needs pressure and a hot nickel catalyst.

name: Glucose respiration
jarvis: Cellular respiration. Your body runs this same reaction thirty seven degrees cooler than a flame would need.
